statement: Let $S$ be a finite set of positive integers with exactly 2023 ordered pairs $(x,y) \in S \times S$ such that $xy$ is a perfect square. Prove one can find at least four distinct elements in $S$ with no pairwise product a perfect square.

Let $a_0,\ldots,a_{100}$ be positive reals. For each $k \in \{0,\ldots,100\}$, consider the polynomial $a_{100+k}x^{100} + 100a_{99+k}x^{99} + a_{98+k}x^{98} + \cdots + a_k$ (indices mod 101). Show it is impossible for all 101 polynomials to have all real roots.
Find all real $c$ for which there exists $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with: $\frac{f(x+a)-f(x)}{a}$ is an integer iff $a=1$; and $|f(x)-cx| < 2023$ for all $x \in \mathbb{N}$.

$2N+1$ coins (all heads) on a circle; Calvin and Hobbes play. Calvin turns a coin to tails; Hobbes may turn at most one adjacent coin from tails to heads. Calvin wins if $k$ coins show tails after Hobbes's move. Find all $k$ for which Calvin wins.
Euler marks $n$ points in the plane. For each pair, Gauss writes $\lfloor \log_2 d \rfloor$ where $d$ is the distance. Prove Gauss writes fewer than $2n$ distinct values.

Euclid has a cyclos: given three non-collinear points, draw their circumcircle; given two points, draw the circle with them as diameter endpoints; mark intersections of circles or a new point on a circle. Show given two marked points, Euclid can draw a circle centered at one passing through the other.
